Notes

脱口而出

脱口而出 means blurting something out, without first thinking or holding it back. The opening treats expression as immediate; later he worries that speaking too much will make him seem self-pitying. The pressure is partly over whether to speak at all.

  • Genius community lyric text
揭不开锅

Literally being unable to lift the pot lid: having no food to cook. Applying it to 心事 (private worries) makes hardship both an unmet material need and a possible store of creative value.

  • Genius community lyric text
矫情

Here 矫情 suggests seeming affected, overdramatic, or excessively self-pitying. The speaker worries about how expressing his trouble will be received, rather than simply saying the trouble is untrue.

  • Genius community lyric text
紧箍咒

In Journey to the West, a spell tightens the band around Sun Wukong’s head, causing pain and compelling obedience. The phrase can describe a constraining rule or pressure; here he likens the repeated nagging to it.

  • Genius community lyric text
  • Journey to the West, chapter 14
把酒言欢

A set phrase for drinking together and talking happily. Between “a short fuse” and “finish this performance,” that polished language of conviviality can sound like a social role being maintained despite irritation.

  • Genius community lyric text
往前走

Asked by Sabukaru how he stays grounded in the music industry, Jackzebra answered in terms of continuing to walk and not looking back. The same plain instruction appears here under a heavy load. The interview is context for a recurring stance, not his explanation of this song.

  • Genius community lyric text
  • Jackzebra interviewed by Sabukaru
对着空气自首

自首 normally means voluntarily surrendering oneself to the authorities or admitting an offense. Addressing empty air removes the person who could hear or judge that admission. After the unclean hands, the legal word turns private unease into an unanswered confession.

  • Genius community lyric text
